candidates.name: Rheumatoid Arthritis
support_spans: symmetric pain in the small joints of her hands, wrists, knees, and ankles
early morning stiffness lasting 2 hours daily
Family history is notable for a maternal aunt with rheumatoid arthritis
contradict_spans: Radiographs of the hands, knees, ankles, and feet were unremarkable
Hand ultrasound showed no joint erosion
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and family history suggest Rheumatoid Arthritis, but the lack of joint erosion on radiographs and ultrasound is not typical of the disease.

candidates.name: Psoriatic Arthritis
support_spans: symmetric pain in the small joints of her hands, wrists, knees, and ankles
early morning stiffness lasting 2 hours daily
contradict_spans: There were no recent genitourinary or gastrointestinal infections and no history of psoriasis or uveitis
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms could suggest Psoriatic Arthritis, but the lack of psoriasis or uveitis in her history makes it less likely.

candidates.name: Rheumatoid Arthritis
support_spans: rheumatoid factor of 62.29 IU/mL (normal <20 IU/mL)
anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody of 237.39 units (normal <20 units)
candidates.why: The presence of rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody suggests an autoimmune mechanism, consistent with Rheumatoid Arthritis.

candidates.name: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
support_spans: antinuclear antibody titer of 1:640
contradict_spans: negative extractable nuclear antigen and double-stranded DNA antibodies
candidates.why: The presence of a high antinuclear antibody titer suggests an autoimmune mechanism, but the lack of other specific antibodies makes Systemic Lupus Erythematosus less likely.

candidates.name: Rheumatoid Arthritis
support_spans: MRI of the hands demonstrated synovitis of the bilateral distal radioulnar joints and the left second metacarpophalangeal joint
candidates.why: The MRI findings of synovitis and tenosynovitis are consistent with Rheumatoid Arthritis, and could be considered decisive in confirming the diagnosis.
